headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: unstructured can read/write files and egress allowlisted data, while plano can ingest and route content via broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Unstructured reads filesystem content and processes documents, so attacker-controlled text could be passed onward as content. Plano can call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and has broad network egress, so if its outputs are bridged into unstructured workflows, prompt-like content may propagate. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than direct.
conditions: IF plano outputs are copied into unstructured input files or pipelines without sanitization, injection risk exists.
IF unstructured treats document text as instructions in a downstream workflow, attacker content can steer processing.
mitigations: Add a strict content/schema separator between model output and document text.
Strip or escape instruction-like text before handing files to unstructured.
Review a sample pipeline for any prompt text embedded in documents.
Use allowlisted templates for any downstream automation.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to distinguish instructions from data.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Unstructured can read and write files and has allowlisted network egress; plano has broad network egress and touches logs, traces, and metrics. If they share a workspace or file handoff, sensitive document content or operational telemetry can flow between them. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default deployments but not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or mounted volume, file contents can cross between them.
IF plano forwards logs/traces to an external service, operational data may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory or container volume.
Disable or minimize telemetry/log export for plano.
Restrict unstructured to a dedicated input folder.
Audit outbound destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Unstructured has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, spawn_subprocesses, and supports multiple instances; plano has broad network egress and no multiple-instance support. If they share mutable files or a workspace, concurrent edits and pipeline races are plausible. There is no locking mechanism documented for the pair, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or partial reads can occur.
IF plano is run alongside another instance despite its single-instance model, state conflicts may arise.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Run only one plano instance per workspace.
Use atomic rename for handoff files.
Check for stale lockfiles before starting jobs.
requires-engineering: add explicit workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Unstructured can transform documents into downstream text, and plano can route or send content through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If unstructured output is treated as authoritative input by plano, errors can cascade into later actions or responses. No verification step is documented between them, so the safer medium severity applies.
conditions: IF unstructured output is fed directly into plano without validation, parsing errors can propagate.
IF plano uses unstructured-derived text as the basis for user-facing responses, mistakes can be amplified.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between extraction and routing.
Compare extracted fields against source documents for a sample batch.
Require human review for high-impact outputs.
Log source-to-output mappings for traceability.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. Plano touches logs/traces/metrics, while unstructured processes documents/images/text, so compliance gaps are possible but not evidenced here. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not documented, low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through plano logs or unstructured document pipelines, policy review is required.
IF the deployment adds a residency or retention constraint not reflected in the profiles, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling for both agents.
Disable retention of sensitive logs where possible.
Review privacy policy and DPA terms before deployment.
Segregate regulated documents from general workloads.
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency controls.
